parts.text: How should she label the venation on each print?

options.text: Spinach print: reticulate venation; grass print: parallel venation.
Spinach print: parallel venation; grass print: reticulate venation.
Both prints show only parallel venation.
Both prints show only reticulate venation.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Charu presses a spinach leaf and a grass blade between notebook pages. On the spinach print she sees a thick middle line with a net of thinner lines on both sides. On the grass print the lines run side by side from base to tip.

part_answers.answer: A net-like pattern beside a thick middle vein is reticulate venation; veins running side by side are parallel venation.

teacher.key_rationale: Net-like veins beside a thick midrib are reticulate; side-by-side veins are parallel. Swapping the labels reverses that relationship.
